Subject: APAC residency evidence request — CAIQ/SIG + private peering details

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick chat yesterday. PacificCare is moving forward with a pilot in APAC and our security/compliance team has a couple of focused asks before we can clear Redwood for private deployments into our VPCs. We're consolidating evidence for CAIQ and SIG reviewers — below are the items they flagged as priority for APAC-only hosting + privatelink:

- CAIQ: the APAC-relevant sections (networking, key management, data locality) — we need the exported matrices and any clarifying notes on assumptions.
- SIG: answers for operator access, key custodians, and evidence of tenant boundary controls.
- Network: list of private peering endpoints (FQDNs/IP ranges), egress routing controls, and fallback policy if an APAC node is degraded.
- KMS/keys: confirmation of regional key partitioning (are keys in APAC physically or logically partitioned), and the roster of keystore operators with role descriptions.

Can you provide the above or point us to a single evidence package? Prefer attachments or a Drive folder we can reference in our questionnaire. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute walk-through with our SIG reviewers next week (APAC-friendly times).

Appreciate it — Jin
Jin Park
Head of Cloud Security
PacificCare Analytics

Jin — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to be transparent. I've attached an evidence packet to get you started: a redacted SOC 2 Type II cover, an APAC-scoped CAIQ export, a CSV with our current private peering endpoints in APAC, and an operator roster template. High level notes up front:

- Residency: Redwood runs APAC inference in isolated AZs in the Singapore region. Data at rest for APAC private deployments is kept within region-local storage; we can provide runbook excerpts that show egress controls and routing policies.
- KMS: We support region-scoped key rings. Keys used for APAC private deployments are logically partitioned and subject to customer KMS integration if you bring your own key. For Redwood-managed keys we can provide the keystore operator roster and rotation cadence.
- Tenant isolation: We use dedicated tenant pools for private deployments and VPC peering is provisioned via customer-controlled peering connections — we never route tenant traffic out of the declared region unless explicit failover is triggered by policy.

Next steps I suggest: 1) Review the attached CAIQ/APAC sheet and SOC2 stub; 2) let us know any SIG control numbers you want us to expand; 3) pick a time for a short walk-through so Ben (infra) and Irene (security ops) can answer detailed operator/KMS questions.

Available times for an APAC-friendly call from our side: Dec 8–10, 09:00–12:00 SGT. Will you and your SIG reviewers have availability?

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Internal: PacificCare — CAIQ/SIG APAC asks (keystore/operator details)

Priyom & Irene — quick responses:

- Peering endpoints: customer-visible endpoints are the privatelink hostnames (privatelink.sg01.redwood.net) and the associated public announcement IP ranges for setup (we provide a small set of routable prefixes used only for peering handshakes). The full internal operator endpoints (control-plane IPs) are internal-only and not shared. I'll attach the CSV that lists the customer-facing hostnames and routable prefixes.
- Failover: by default we fail over to a warm-standby in the neighboring APAC AZ in the same region (no cross-border traffic for failover unless the customer explicitly enables global-fallback).
- KMS/key partitioning: keys are logically partitioned per region. For BYOK customers we provide a key handle and never export plaintext key material. Rotation: automated quarterly rotation with MFA-protected operator authorization for emergency rotations.

Attaching: privatelink_endpoints_apac.csv (customer hostnames + prefixes)

Ben
Ben Carter
